Open a table

Source: R/open.R
lake_open.Rd

lake_open() builds a snapshot of a Delta Lake table: one version of it, replayed from the table's own log as the Delta protocol prescribes. A snapshot never changes; lake_load() builds another one of the same table, at another version or at the version the log now ends at.

Usage

lake_open(uri, version = NULL, timestamp = NULL, credentials = NULL)

lake_load(tbl, version = NULL, timestamp = NULL)

lake_version(tbl)

Arguments

uri

Location of the table: the path of its directory, the one that holds _delta_log/.

version

Version to open, a whole number. NULL, the default, is the latest version.

timestamp

Open the latest version committed at or before this time, a POSIXct. The commit time is the commit's in-commit timestamp when the table records them, and the commit file's modification time otherwise. A time before the first commit opens the first version. Give version or timestamp, not both.

credentials

A function of no arguments returning a bearer token, for tables on Azure. Not used for local paths.

tbl

A snapshot, from lake_open() or lake_load().

Value

lake_open() and lake_load() return a snapshot, an object of class zulake_table. lake_version() returns the version a snapshot holds, a whole number as a double.

Every error is a condition of class zulake_error, with a subclass that says why: zulake_error_not_table (no Delta log at uri), zulake_error_version (no such version), zulake_error_corrupt_log (a log that breaks the protocol, such as a commit that is not JSON or a partition value of the wrong type), zulake_error_checkpoint_unreadable and zulake_error_unsupported_feature, whose feature field names the feature.

Details

The snapshot holds the version's protocol, metadata, live files, tombstones, application transactions and metadata domains. It is checked before it is returned: a table that needs a reader feature zulake does not support is refused with an error naming that feature, before any data file is read, because ignoring a feature returns wrong rows.

In this version zulake reads tables on local disk, replaying the log from its first commit. A table whose log no longer reaches commit 0 needs a checkpoint, which zulake cannot read yet, and is refused with a zulake_error_checkpoint_unreadable error.

See also

lake_is_table() to check a location first.

Examples

# A one-file table written by hand, so the example needs nothing else.
path <- tempfile("table")
dir.create(file.path(path, "_delta_log"), recursive = TRUE)
writeLines(c(
  '{"protocol":{"minReaderVersion":1,"minWriterVersion":2}}',
  paste0(
    '{"metaData":{"id":"example","format":{"provider":"parquet","options":{}},',
    '"schemaString":"{\\"type\\":\\"struct\\",\\"fields\\":[{\\"name\\":',
    '\\"id\\",\\"type\\":\\"long\\",\\"nullable\\":true,\\"metadata\\":{}}]}",',
    '"partitionColumns":[],"configuration":{}}}'
  ),
  paste0(
    '{"add":{"path":"part-0.parquet","partitionValues":{},"size":100,',
    '"modificationTime":0,"dataChange":true}}'
  )
), file.path(path, "_delta_log", "00000000000000000000.json"))

lake_is_table(path)
#> [1] TRUE
tbl <- lake_open(path)
lake_version(tbl)
#> [1] 0
tbl0 <- lake_load(tbl, version = 0)

unlink(path, recursive = TRUE)
